question: Which of the following responses is characteristic of captopril:

options.opa: It acts as a prodrug that requires prior transformation at the liver level.
options.opb: Causes a competitive blockage of the AT1 receiver.
options.opc: Reduces the concentration of renin in blood.
options.opd: It has shown efficacy in the prevention of diabetic nephropathy.

analysis: Captopril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor used primarily for the treatment of hypertension and heart failure. It is not a prodrug, as it is active in its administered form, unlike some other ACE inhibitors. Captopril does not block the AT1 receptor; instead, it inhibits the conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, which indirectly reduces the effects mediated by the AT1 receptor. It does not directly reduce renin concentration; in fact, ACE inhibitors can lead to an increase in plasma renin activity due to feedback mechanisms. Captopril has been shown to be effective in the prevention of diabetic nephropathy by reducing intraglomerular pressure and proteinuria, which is a characteristic response of this medication.
